documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 03/19/2026; date of service 03/10/2026)

CC: shortness of breath and seizure after delivery.

HPI: 34 y/o G3, term, brought in by EMS about half an hour after a rapid spontaneous vaginal delivery before arrival (liveborn infant). Shortly after the birth she became acutely dyspneic and had seizures witnessed by EMS. Background of chronic hypertension on labetalol, a placental abruption in 2023, and amniotic fluid embolism after her delivery in 01/2025.
Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis) - latex-free room.
Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, prenatal vitamin with DHA, folic acid 1 mg.

Exam: BP 70/40, HR 120, RR 30, SpO2 85% on room air. Not protecting her airway. Rales throughout both lung fields. Petechiae across the chest and both arms.

Course: intubated for airway protection. Labs: Hgb 9.0 g/dL (ref 12-16), platelets 50K (ref 150-400K), PT 18 s (ref 12-15), aPTT 40 s (ref 30-40), fibrinogen 100 mg/dL (ref 200-400), D-dimer elevated. Bedside echo: no right heart strain. Aggressive crystalloid and blood product resuscitation, yet she continued to decline. OB and critical care at bedside.

Impression: recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with disseminated intravascular coagulation and hypovolemic shock.
Disposition: ICU.

events.reason: Recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and shock

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 03/19/2026)
Admitted 03/10/2026 via the ED. Discharged 03/18/2026.

Principal diagnosis: amniotic fluid embolism, recurrent (prior episode 01/2025).
Secondary: disseminated intravascular coagulation; hypovolemic shock.
Background: chronic hypertension; anxiety disorder; placental abruption 10/2023 with emergency cesarean; laparoscopic appendectomy.
Allergies: sulfonamides - rash; latex - contact dermatitis.

Hospital course: Arrived intubated from the ED after a precipitous term delivery before arrival, with hypoxemia, seizures, shock and consumptive coagulopathy. In the ICU, resuscitation with blood products continued until bleeding and coagulation studies corrected; blood pressure recovered over the first day. No further seizure activity. Extubated 03/12 without difficulty. Moved to the postpartum unit 03/14 and progressed well. Hemoglobin stable on the last two checks before discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged): labetalol 200 mg PO BID; prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; folic acid 1 mg daily.

Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with CBC, CMP and coagulation studies; obstetric postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Dear Colleague,

Tessa Turcotte was seen on 04/22/2026 for her postpartum visit after delivery on 03/10/2026 complicated by recurrent amniotic fluid embolism with DIC and shock requiring ICU care. She is recovering well. Lochia has resolved and her exam is unremarkable. Blood pressure is controlled on labetalol 200 mg twice daily, which remains under your management.

Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).

Thank you for sharing her care.

Obstetrics
